newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares mixed, profit take in blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares mixed, profit take in blue chips.

text.p: Singapore shares were mixed at the open on Wednesday with light profit taking seen in selected blue chips after recent gains.
Singapore Press foreign was down 50 cents to Singapore $30.10, OCBC foreign and UOB foreign were also down 40 cents to S$15.20 and 30 cents to S$16.10 respectively.
But activity and interest in electronics stocks continued to be brisk with the SES Electronics index up 1.63 points or 1.26 percent to 131.02 after an hour of trading.
"There is quite a bit of interest still in electronic stocks and laggards in the sector are picking up," said a trader with a Singapore firm.
Heading actives was sound-card Aztech Systems which gained three cents to Singapore $0.565 on volume of about 2.47 million shares including a married block 838,000 shares at S$0.526.
NatSteel continued to climb in active dealings and was up six cents to S$4.14 after it said it was buying out its partner in a precast concrete and plaster venture.
Electronics based Sunright hit a new high of S$2.73 after a block of 722,000 shares changed hands at S$2.68.
The Straits Times Industrial index was off 5.70 points to 2,001.53. Total market volume was 44 million shares with 123 gainers against 83 losers.
